provider: controlled-command fixture; no live-model reasoning test
workerLifecycle: After checking each of the first two controlled outputs, the fixture explicitly stopped that worker before reviewed integration and scheduling the next. This does not prove natural task exit or automatic capacity release.
failure: Transport evidence buffer reached its 1000-record bound and dropped 27 observations after the third worker started. The workflow correctly refused to pass.
completedChecks: Browser authorized five named tasks across four reviewed projects.
Two actual Docker/Codex commands produced task-scoped outputs from captured context; fixture review/integration checks passed.
A service restart retained the exact live child without replaying the controlled provider.
Browser cancellation of extra waiting work was observed; the final transport ledger was incomplete, so no complete run-wide absence-of-side-effects claim is made.
baseline: post-start; no pre-run idle baseline observed
sampling: One-second target; actual sample gaps are reported. Observation starts after driver spawn, and includes a post-driver-exit settle interval.
limitations: Sum of process RSS double-counts shared pages; it is not unique physical memory.
Container cgroup memory is separate and must not be added to container process RSS.
Docker daemon/shared kernel/VM overhead is unassigned; host memory includes unrelated work.
Processes starting and exiting between 1 Hz samples may be missed; delta counters cover observed intervals only.
Post-driver-exit settlement is not an application idle baseline.
No UI input latency, other-app responsiveness or model reasoning quality is measured.
Initial 39 samples lacked the exact worker-instance identifier; Docker ownership was unavailable during those samples.
Only 14 samples contained running-worker memory, and the third worker had one memory sample.
Short transient processes and worker peaks may fall between observations.
Small controlled tasks and manual worker stops do not establish realistic build capacity or automatic completion.
privacy: Published with an explicit field allowlist. Original PID/starttime, sandbox/container/instance IDs, fixture paths, command lines, environment values, credentials and raw failure stack are omitted. Worker aliases preserve ordering only.
